title: Aromatic Substitution
description: Benzene will not add to itself, but it will swap a hydrogen for a stronger electrophile: a nitronium ion from mixed acid, a diazonium salt, a bromine. What is already on the ring decides how fast, and where. Hammett found one rule for all of it: each substituent has a number σ, each reaction a number ρ, and the rate is multiplied by ten to the σρ. How strong the acid is counts too, beyond what pH can say: Hammett's acidity H₀. Unlocks the Substituent Bench.

puzzle.goal: A substituent with constant σ changes the rate of a reaction with constant ρ. Write the rate k against the rate k0 of plain benzene (Hammett).
puzzle.name: Hammett equation
puzzle.ask: Find k for k0 = 1, σ = @{s} and ρ = −6.
puzzle.method: log(k/k0) is linear in σ: the free energy of the transition state shifts in proportion to how the substituent pushes or pulls charge.
